name: Ideal Final Result (TRIZ)
description: State the ideal and work backwards to a solution
whenToUse: When a target image is needed to work backwards from towards a solution — not to judge a solution already found or to pick between variants.
systemPlaceholder: e.g. belt conveyor for bulk solids
usefulPlaceholder: e.g. transports material from A to B
harmfulPlaceholder: e.g. material jams at the transition and blocks the conveyor
ifrHint: Three increasingly radical ideal statements. Deliberately psychologically uncomfortable — that is where the insight comes from.
ifr1Title: The system solves the problem itself
ifr1Desc: The system remains; the harmful effect disappears without a new mechanism.
ifr1Placeholder: e.g. The conveyor itself prevents jamming.
ifr2Desc: The useful function exists without the system being present at all.
ifr2Placeholder: e.g. The material does not jam. (The problem ceases to exist.)
ifr3Title: A supersystem resource performs the function
ifr3Desc: A resource already present in the environment takes over — for free, no new component.
ifr3Placeholder: e.g. Gravity orients the particles with no intervention.
obstaclesHint: What blocks the system from reaching the IFR today? This list is the actual task list.
obstaclesPlaceholder:
• particle size distribution too wide
• transition angle too steep
• …
openResourcesHint: Add the "Resources Checklist (TRIZ)" module from the extras tile (⋯) — IFR-3 asks for exactly these resources.
